newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Newcrest shares mauled after poor quarter.
newsitem.headline: Newcrest shares mauled after poor quarter.

text.p: Shares in gold miner Newcrest Mining Ltd slumped over eight percent on Thursday to hit A$3.50, their lowest level since September 1993, following Wednesday's disappointing third quarter report.
The company reported a net loss of A$7.1 million for the three months to March 31 and forecast a small full year loss before abnormals.
Heavy rains around its Telfer operation in Western Australia, necessitating a six-week curtailment of mining activities, were cited as the reasons for the reduced revenue and extra costs.
Newcrest said some 20,000 ounces of gold was lost in the quarter due to the closure of Telfer access road and the milling of lower grade ore.
The company also said that delayed work on leach pads would cause production shortfalls of up to 25,000 ounces over the next six months.

"People are obviously unhappy with the quarterly. They have had rain problems which have cut production and costs are looking a bit high," said a Brisbane-based dealer, noting that investors had reassessed their position on the miner.
"There has been a re-rating by some investors and that has led to a pretty severe selloff."
By 3.35 p.m. (0535 GMT), Newcrest shares had lost further ground, down 33 cents at A$3.48 on turnover of 1.6 million shares.
